still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
DOT has still not ruled on incretin use for alcohol reduction or calm-plan use among commercial drivers, and the Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 37.6% ever-used − 28.0% current = 9.6% of adults used and are off now. About 45% of current users are on a second or later course (12.6 pts; public coverage restarted many 2032 stoppers), and 2.6 pts cycled and are off again, so (12.6 + 2.6) / 37.6 ≈ 40% of ever-users have cycled. The rest of the off-now group (9.6 − 2.6 = 7.0 pts) stopped once and did not restart. Current first-course users = 28.0 − 12.6 = 15.4 pts, ~7.8 of them first-timers since 2032 (ever-used rose 8.8 pts, ~1.0 of those already stopped). This fits one-year persistence still near one-third on weekly and oral products (~60% on clinic MariTide, ~55% in Medicare's first benefit year, where step-therapy orals at a $35–60 copay cut cost dropout) and 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×16 + 0.33×26.5 + 0.24×37 + 0.23×31 = 3.2 + 8.7 + 8.9 + 7.1 ≈ 28.0. Income thirds average 28.0. About 28.0% of ~275M adults is ~77.0M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~21.5M (27.9%): ~12.0M on the older diabetes/CV/CKD/OSA/dementia-risk codes plus ~9.5M enrolled in the new obesity benefit by Dec 2034. About 2.5M Medicare users are under-65 disabled, so ~19.0M are 65+, and another ~0.6M 65+ adults pay cash or buy gray: 19.6M / ~63M ≈ 31%. Medicaid ~8.5M (11.0%). HRSA free provision at FQHCs ~2.5M (3.2%). Commercial ~15.5M (20.1%). Legitimate cash (TrumpRx/direct/telehealth, including ~1.9M calm-plan subscribers) ~22.5M (29.2%). Imported or counterfeit ~6.5M (8.4%, down from 7.5M). Public payers together are ~32.5M (42%), the largest payer block. The bottom third's gain (14 → 25) comes mostly through Medicaid, HRSA and dual-eligible Medicare, so it is less gray-market-dependent than in 2032. Gray use now concentrates in the 24 non-expansion states. Adult obesity is ~31.9%. About 16% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in Mississippi, Texas, Georgia and Florida, among men 18–29 and among the uninsured above 200% FPL. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s are on a drug, ~3.1% of 12–17s, and ~0.22% of 6–11s take daily liraglutide (under-12 starts flat since the 2032 growth communication). About 29M children live with at least one parent on a drug, and ~5M with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare Part D covers obesity from Jan 2034 under the Metabolic Health Access Act (Jul 2033). Eligibility is BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. Step therapy starts with oral semaglutide or Foundayo, and injectables follow at <5% loss after 6 months. Users 65+ need a baseline DXA, and an annual lifestyle-and-strength counselling visit is required. Negotiated net is $195/month. FICTIONAL arithmetic: run-rate obesity benefit 9.5M × $195 × 12 ≈ $22.2B/yr. Calendar-2034 obesity spend at ~5.2M average enrolment × $195 × 12 ≈ $12.2B. Older codes 12.0M × ~$220 × 12 ≈ $31.7B. Total Medicare incretin run-rate ≈ $53.9B before rebate true-up. CBO scored the benefit at ≈$186B over 2034–43: ~9.5M average users × ~$175 average declining net × 12 × 10 ≈ $199.5B, plus ~$9B for DXA and Strong Start, minus ~$22B scored offsets. Medicaid gets a 90% FMAP for weight-management coverage, and 26 states now cover weight use, up from 7 (Tennessee, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Arizona among the new ones; Mississippi, Texas, Florida and Georgia did not opt in). About 5.0M new weight-code Medicaid users × $195 × 12 ≈ $11.7B, federal share ≈ $10.5B. The other ~3.5M Medicaid users are on diabetes codes at regular match. Four state programmes condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. HRSA free provision: uninsured adults ≤200% FPL get oral Wegovy or Foundayo free at FQHCs, ~2.5M × $149 × 12 ≈ $4.5B on a $5B/yr appropriation, with the remainder for staffing and DXA vouchers.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across 120+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $15–50, and retatrutide-analogue 'reta' vials appeared in 2033 at $40–90. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China supply about 70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued. TrumpRx maintenance prices are $179 for the Wegovy pill, $139–199 for Foundayo above its $149 starting dose, and $229–279 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound. MariTide direct is $229. Retatrutide keeps flat $1,299 list pricing across doses, ~$349 cash direct including the 12 mg dose. The Medicare and Medicaid net of $195 sits inside the $150–300 brand band, and HRSA buys orals at the $149 starting price. Medicare Part D copays for step-one orals run $35–60 a month under the indexed ~$2,100 out-of-pocket cap. Employer coverage edged up to 31%, because some firms re-added coverage for under-65 staff once retirees moved to Medicare. ~6.4M enrollees are in monitored metabolic tracks, all inside the 15.5M commercial users, and ~4.4M of them are on clinic MariTide (~6.1M MariTide users in total). Orals are ~52% of users, pushed up by Medicare step therapy and HRSA. The gray market fell to ~6.5M users. It is concentrated in non-expansion states, among the uninsured above HRSA's income line and among people seeking 30% results at gray prices. Telegram 'reta' shops are the growth segment.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose approved Aug 2033)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; Pausa for alcohol use disorder, approved Nov 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Adjunct: activin type II receptor antibody, IV every 4 weeks (bimagrumab), for lean-mass preservation in incretin users 60+ with low muscle mass (approved Jun 2033)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; growth-monitoring label)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial readout slipped to 2035)
alcohol use disorder: reduction in heavy drinking days (oral semaglutide, branded Pausa, Nov 2033), the first approved reward-modulation indication
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' telehealth plans (low-dose oral semaglutide, Foundayo and now off-label Pausa), ~1.9M subscribers, down from a mid-2033 peak of ~2.2M
Pausa prescribed off-label for gambling, nicotine, compulsive shopping and 'motivation' complaints
planned 'drug holidays' and dose-downs around weddings, holidays, vacations and creative deadlines
dementia-prevention use by 60–70-year-olds without CVD, now mostly absorbed into Medicare's obesity benefit where BMI qualifies
microdosing for 'steadiness' recommended by employer wellness coaches
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label, low and flat)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Lilly filed an sNDA in Sep 2032 for a retatrutide 12 mg maintenance dose on TRIUMPH data. It was approved Aug 2033 at ~29% mean loss at 80 weeks (efficacy estimand; ~27% treatment-regimen), with dysaesthesia and heart-rate language. This realises the triple_agonist_30pct driver as an existing product in a new dose. Oral semaglutide for AUD (filed Jan 2032) was approved Nov 2033 and launched Jan 2034 as Pausa. Its label is heavy-drinking-day reduction, and craving scores are secondary endpoints. This realises mood_and_motivation through an approved reward-modulation indication that Novo markets as 'quiet the pull'. No 'mood' or 'focus' indication exists. Bimagrumab (filed Jul 2032) was approved Jun 2033 as an adjunct, at ~$849/month list, with ~2–3 kg lean mass preserved in trials and no fracture-endpoint data. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial slipped to 2035. Implant programmes remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the market. Oral amycretin is in phase 3. No oral matches tirzepatide. The global incretin market is ~$205B (2033). US net prices drift down 4–6% a year, and brands hold above ~$150.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Rates are higher on retatrutide 12 mg. Medicare's first-year users report it most in the first 8 weeks.
Elevated with rapid weight loss, and higher at 12 mg retatrutide.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation continues to centre on EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR is ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Hip BMD falls ~1.5–2%/yr in users 65+ vs ~0.5% in controls. EPI adds to the risk through vitamin D/K malabsorption. This entry became a population problem in 2033 (see the hip-fracture entry below).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Upgraded to Warnings and Precautions (Oct 2033). Baseline DXA is required for users 65+ and repeated every 2 years for long-term users. Resistance-training counselling is on all class labels. Bimagrumab is approved as an adjunct.

safety_ledger.effect: Population-level hip-fracture and sarcopenia burden in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: In May 2033 CDC/NCHS reported the first rise in age-adjusted hip-fracture hospitalisations among Americans 65+ in three decades, up ~6% from 2030 to 2032. A CMS analysis attributed ~14,000 excess hip fractures a year to incretin use: ~12M users 65+ × ~0.4% baseline × 0.3 excess. Sarcopenia diagnosis codes roughly doubled. With 65+ users rising toward ~19.6M, the excess projects toward ~23,000 a year unless mitigation works. Hip fractures carry ~20% one-year mortality, and analysts disagree on how much the drugs' CV and dementia benefits offset this.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning upgrade (Oct 2033). Medicare's obesity benefit requires baseline DXA and an annual strength-counselling visit and funds Strong Start supervised training. AGS/Endocrine Society joint statement favours slower titration and protein targets in 65+. DXA waits run 6–10 weeks in Sun Belt retirement metros.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including in the FDA anhedonia study.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (Sep 2033, n≈410,000) found clinically meaningful anhedonia at HR ~2.1 on maintenance doses (~7% vs ~3.3%) and ~10–11% on retatrutide 12 mg. At low 'calm' doses the HR was ~1.3, with a CI touching 1. It is observational, not randomised, and partial recovery comes within weeks of a pause.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Anhedonia added to adverse reactions on all class labels (Dec 2033), with no boxed or W&P warning. The Pausa label carries it from launch. OMA guidance (2034) describes dose-down and planned-pause protocols. Calm-plan claims remain under untitled letters only.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Short planned holidays of under 2 weeks show little regain.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing and Medicare's continuation rules.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Protein insufficiency in older users is now linked to the fracture burden.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; Medicare covers the panel under the benefit.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Semaglutide ~2× (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years) after 5+ years. Tirzepatide 6-year data show a ~1.4× excess that is now nominally significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class EPI warning retained. FDA opened a tirzepatide labelling review in 2034.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Drug-holiday patterns add a new cycling form whose bone and pancreatic effects are uncharacterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue. FDA asked sponsors for pause-pattern data in postmarketing studies.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~31,000 by mid-2034. There was no new mass cluster in the window, only scattered contamination and mislabelled 'reta' vials. Poison-centre calls are flat at ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts maintained. The Act funds CBP mail screening and requires domestic fill-finish for HRSA purchases. Personal-importation statute unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month liraglutide PMR update (2034) shows height velocity still ~0.6 cm/yr below expected in prepubertal starters, with partial catch-up in those who stopped. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8 and unchanged. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA label monitoring unchanged and no age restriction. EMA (2033) restricted under-12 initiation to specialist centres. AAP lifestyle-first guidance stands.

safety_ledger.effect: High-dose triple-agonist effects (dysaesthesia, resting heart-rate rise, arrhythmia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Dysaesthesia/skin-sensitivity in ~15–20% on retatrutide 12 mg, mostly mild. Resting heart rate +5–7 bpm. Arrhythmia reports are under evaluation, with no confirmed excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled in adverse reactions. Cardiac-rhythm postmarketing requirement issued with the Aug 2033 approval.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~14% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~12%. Dollar sales slipped ~1–2% in 2034 as mix gains slowed. The Medicare benefit created a senior segment: Abbott and Nestlé Health Science report double-digit growth in high-protein oral nutrition shakes, and pharmacies stock 'Strong Start' protein bays next to the Part D counter. Kroger's zip-code planning now keys on Medicare density as well as income. Whey tightened again in 2034 on senior demand.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~17% from 2025 and beer ~11%. Pausa's launch and off-label prescribing hit heavy-drinker volume further. Constellation and Molson Coors cut Midwest capacity. Weekend and holiday spikes are visible in scanner data as users time drug pauses around occasions. Non-alcoholic lines grow but remain small.

restaurants.state: Traffic is down ~2% over two years. Weekday checks are smaller, and Friday–Sunday and holiday-week checks are disproportionately large as diners pause their dose. Darden and Cheesecake Factory market 'off-week' tasting menus. Senior-heavy markets (Mesa, The Villages) report smaller early-bird portions. QSR value menus hold in non-expansion-state markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue shrinking. Mass retailers set size runs by zip code and now by Medicare-age share. Senior 'refit' tailoring and adaptive wear grow. Resale and stretch serve cyclers.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth market. Medicare's Strong Start benefit pays for 24 supervised resistance sessions a year for obesity-benefit enrollees, and YMCAs, Planet Fitness senior hours and physical-therapy chains are the main vendors. Premium DXA-plus-coaching runs $250–400 a month. DXA scanner orders doubled, and technicians are short.

insurance.state: Medicare Part D: CMS ran a one-year federal reinsurance for 2034 because plan bids predated the Act. The 2035 base beneficiary premium rose ~11%, about half attributed to incretins. Commercial pharmacy trend ~+5%, and employer coverage edged to 31% as retirees moved to Medicare. Adherence-premium vendors added 'holiday codes' allowing two registered pauses a quarter, and not all employers accept them. Some life insurers ask off-drug applicants with obesity history why they stopped.

pharma.state: Volume rose ~45% in two years while US net prices fell ~10%. Lilly leads on retatrutide 12 mg and tirzepatide, Novo on orals, Medicare step therapy and Pausa, and Amgen on employer clinic tracks. Bimagrumab is a small, slow launch, held back by DXA bottlenecks and prior authorisation. Global market ~$205B (2033). Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being medicated no longer signals anything. Being visibly off does: a regained body in an office or a doctor's waiting room invites the question 'what happened?' Muscle on an older body now reads as coached and scanned. A stooped, thin 70-year-old reads as a fracture risk, and grandchildren are told to watch the stairs.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The income gap in use narrowed (top 31%, bottom 25%), but the class marker moved from whether you are on it to what you are on and what surrounds it. In Charlotte and Austin the boast is retatrutide 12 mg plus a coach, or 'off-drug lean'. In Mesa and Sun City, Arizona, the Medicare benefit made the Foundayo pill and the Tuesday Strong Start class a retiree routine. Memphis, in Tennessee's expansion, saw gray use fall. Across the river in Mississippi, which did not opt in, the cycler body remains the visible norm in the Delta.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Weekday meals are small and quick. Weekends and holidays have become feast occasions planned around dose pauses, and hosts ask 'are you on or off this week?' as routinely as about allergies. The Bread Alone fasting network claims ~700 congregations and added a 'Sabbath pause' teaching. School-weight reporting debates continue without federal action.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Being on is assumed, so profiles that say 'off by choice' attract both curiosity and suspicion. Couples sync their drug holidays ('sync weeks') for anniversaries and travel. 'Lean-mass verified' badges persist as a premium tier.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a dial. People turn it down for the week and back up for an occasion. Never using a drug now needs explaining at the doctor's, and stopping needs explaining at work and to family. Unmuted reframed itself around the right to be off without penalty. MAHA claims Strong Start as its win, and fat-acceptance groups remain separate.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Sep 2033 FDA observational study puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7% of maintenance-dose users vs ~3.3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide 12 mg and ~4% at low calm doses. With ~77M users, that implies roughly 3M people with an excess blunting burden. In a 2034 KFF survey, 38% of users report at least one planned drug holiday that year, and 22% report a dose-down for 'feeling flat'. Calm plans fell from a ~2.2M peak to ~1.9M. Pausa reached ~0.9M users in its first year.
interior_life.framing: Mostly treated as a side effect that can be managed. 'Flat' is ordinary conversation, and 'take a week off' is ordinary advice. Novo markets Pausa as 'quiet the pull', and telehealth calm plans now advertise 'holidays built in'. Clinicians speak of dose titration to affect. Unmuted calls the holiday a ration of feeling.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~6.4M workers are in adherence-verified tracks, and 'holiday codes' decide whether a pause costs premium. Creative and sales staff schedule pauses before pitches and deadlines ('I need my edge'), while some managers prefer staff 'on' during audits. One of the two EEOC ADA charges received a right-to-sue letter, and a suit is pending in the Southern District of Ohio.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-week' is a genre: festivals, gallery openings and tasting menus schedule for pause weekends. 'Flat' fiction is fading, and the bestseller is the holiday diary. Sportsbook handle shows weekend spikes during pause weeks. Ambient streaming targeting continues.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the top couples' complaint. Sync weeks are the common workaround. Therapists report partners negotiating which one stays on during a pause week to keep weight or drinking in check.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Metabolic Health Access Act passed with bipartisan majorities and is popular with seniors ahead of the 2034 midterms. Budget hawks now campaign on the 2035 Part D premium rise. The children question has stalled. Blunting is discussed as a consumer complaint, not a civic one, and no turnout effect has been shown.

state.regulatory_posture: Active and accommodating. FDA approved bimagrumab (Jun 2033), retatrutide 12 mg (Aug 2033) and oral semaglutide for AUD as Pausa (Nov 2033). It upgraded the lean-mass/bone warning and added anhedonia to adverse reactions, and it took no enforcement action on calm-plan marketing. Congress passed the Metabolic Health Access Act (Jul 2033). Illinois remains the only state banning adherence-conditioned premiums.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Metabolic Health Access Act provides: a Medicare Part D obesity benefit from Jan 2034 at a $195 negotiated net, with step therapy, a baseline DXA for 65+ and annual counselling; a 90% FMAP for state Medicaid weight-management coverage, taken up by 26 states; and HRSA free oral provision for uninsured adults ≤200% FPL at FQHCs on a $5B/yr appropriation (FY2034–36), restricted to products filled and finished in the US. The Strong Start supervised-training benefit was a MAHA concession. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare continuation requires documented counselling visits and, for 65+, DXA, and these records flow to Part D plans. Four Medicaid programmes condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress, and OBBBA work requirements apply in addition. Employer wellness vendors log registered drug holidays. Telehealth calm platforms still sell de-identified mood cohorts to benefit brokers.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE for Life follows Medicare as secondary payer, so military retirees 65+ gained the benefit automatically. Active-duty TRICARE rules are unchanged, and the Army recruit oral pilot is not expanded. DOT has still not ruled on alcohol-reduction or calm-plan use among commercial drivers, now including on-label Pausa.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply ~70% of world volume. The Act's domestic fill-finish rule for HRSA purchases favours Lilly's and Novo's US plants, and New Delhi called it a trade barrier. US–India talks still have no mail-enforcement agreement. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: CDC reports the first rise in age-adjusted hip-fracture hospitalisations among Americans 65+ in three decades; a CMS analysis attributes ~14,000 excess fractures a year to incretin use, and in October FDA upgrades the class warning and requires baseline DXA for users 65 and older

Congress passes the Metabolic Health Access Act in a health-extenders package: Medicare Part D covers obesity drugs from January 2034 at a $195 negotiated net, Medicaid gets a 90% match for weight coverage, HRSA gets $5B a year for free pills at community health centres, and a supervised strength-training benefit is added at MAHA legislators' insistence
events.driver: coverage_shift: public_expansion; state_action: subsidy; price_path: managed_decline

events.event: FDA approves a 12 mg maintenance dose of Lilly's retatrutide after trials showing ~29% average weight loss at 80 weeks; Lilly keeps flat $1,299 list pricing and $349 direct cash, and 'reta' copies appear on Telegram within weeks

FDA's postmarketing study of 410,000 users finds clinically meaningful anhedonia roughly doubled at maintenance doses and slightly raised at low doses; anhedonia is added to all class labels in December, and obesity-medicine guidance on dose-downs and planned pauses follows

FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder; Novo launches it in January 2034 under the separate brand Pausa with the campaign 'Quiet the pull', and telehealth calm platforms begin prescribing it off-label for gambling and 'motivation'

CMS says 9.5 million beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare's obesity benefit in its first ten months, taking use among Americans 65+ past 30%; a KFF poll finds 57% of adults think a person with obesity who is not on a drug should have to explain why to their doctor

open_tensions: Medicare is enrolling millions of older adults during a recognised fracture wave. DXA waits run up to ten weeks in retirement metros, bimagrumab reaches few people, and excess hip fractures are projected toward ~23,000 a year unless Strong Start and slower titration work.

Blunting is now a mainstream complaint managed by planned pauses. Adherence-premium systems and Medicare continuation rules count pauses as gaps, and Novo markets reward modulation as 'quiet the pull'.
Public payers now cover 42% of users. The 2035 Part D premium rise, a ~$54B Medicare incretin run-rate and the $186B CBO score give budget hawks a target just as the benefit becomes popular.

The 24 non-expansion states and uninsured adults above HRSA's income line hold most of the 6.5M gray-market users, now chasing 30% results through 'reta' vials. The children's final height is still unknown.

prose.headline: Medicare Pays, Grandpa Lifts: The Year Being Off the Drug Became the Thing You Have to Explain
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about seventy-seven million American adults take an incretin drug, more than one in four. Being on one is no longer news. Not being on one is what people ask about. Doctors ask it of patients with obesity who have never started. Managers ask it of a colleague who has regained. Life insurers ask it of applicants whose history shows a stop.

The largest change is who pays. In July 2033 Congress passed the Metabolic Health Access Act. The country had been absorbing the gray market's deaths, manufacturers had offered a Medicare net price of $195 a month, and seniors would vote in the 2034 midterms. From January, Medicare Part D covers obesity itself. Medicaid gets a ninety-percent federal match for weight coverage, and twenty-six states took it. Community health centres hand out oral Wegovy and Foundayo free to uninsured adults near the poverty line. Public programmes now pay for about four users in ten, more than employers or cash. Nine and a half million beneficiaries enrolled in ten months. CBO put the decade's cost near $186 billion, and the 2035 Part D premium has already risen about eleven percent.

The benefit came with conditions written after a bad spring. In May 2033 the CDC reported that hip-fracture hospitalisations among older Americans had risen for the first time in thirty years. Medicare's own analysis attributed about fourteen thousand excess fractures a year to the drugs. The FDA strengthened its warning and required a bone scan before anyone over sixty-five starts. MAHA legislators, who had opposed paying for the drugs at all, traded their votes for Strong Start, twenty-four supervised strength sessions a year. So retirees in Mesa take a pill at breakfast and a resistance class on Tuesdays, and the bone-scan waits in Phoenix are ten weeks. A muscle-preserving antibody was approved in June 2033. Few people get it.

At the top of the market, Lilly's retatrutide gained a higher dose in August 2033 that takes off nearly thirty percent of body weight. It costs $349 a month in cash and carries a new list of side effects about skin sensitivity and heart rate. Copies called 'reta' were on Telegram within weeks. The gray market shrank to six and a half million users. Most of them live in states that refused the Medicaid match, like Mississippi, where the cycler's body is still the familiar one. Across the river in Memphis, Tennessee's expansion has pulled people onto pharmacy shelves.

The feeling problem now has a name everyone uses. In September 2033 the FDA's long-awaited study confirmed what users had been saying. At maintenance doses, roughly twice as many people as expected lose a real share of pleasure, and more do on the strongest drugs. The labels now say so. The common answer is the drug holiday: a week off before a wedding, a pitch or an anniversary. More than a third of users took one this year. Restaurants sell off-week tasting menus. Couples sync their pauses. Employers' wellness vendors log holidays as codes, and whether a code costs premium depends on the company.

At the same moment the reward effect became a product with a label. Novo's oral semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder and launched as Pausa under the line 'Quiet the pull'. Telehealth calm plans prescribe it off-label for gambling and motivation. Nearly a million people took Pausa in its first year, and fewer bought calm plans than at their 2033 peak.

The children's question has not moved. Kids who started before puberty still grow more slowly, and nobody knows their adult height. The country looks steadier and leaner, with older people lifting weights. It is also more fragile in the hip, and it now schedules its pleasures a week at a time.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Ocampo takes the Foundayo at six with half a glass of water, standing, because the counselling sheet says standing. The bottle says $47. Lorraine's bottle sits beside his, the Wegovy pill, $179 on her card because she is sixty-four and the government says wait.

She has hers in her hand and doesn't take it. 'Quinceañera Saturday,' she says. 'I'm on holiday.' She puts it back.

At the Mesa community centre the Tuesday class is nine men and fourteen women on benches. The trainer, Keisha, is twenty-six and carries a tablet that pings Ray's Part D plan when she taps his name. Goblet squats with an eight-kilo kettlebell. Ray's T-score was minus 1.8. He watches the stairs on the way out like everyone does now.

In the parking lot Hector Ruiz, eighty-one, leans on his car. He used to be big. Now he is big again. 'You on it?' Ray asks, then wishes he hadn't.

'Cardiologist took me off. The scan.' Hector taps his hip. 'They want me on the muscle one. The prior auth's been in since March.'

Ray drinks his protein shake in the truck. Strawberry, from the Walgreens bay with the Strong Start sign. It tastes like a pharmacy.

At home Lorraine has the stove going: real chorizo, a whole pan of it. She is humming. He hasn't heard her hum since spring.

'Taste,' she says, holding out a spoon.

He tastes it. It's good. He knows it's good. He tries to feel how good, and it's quiet, like a song playing in another room.

'Ray,' she says. 'Take a week off with me.'
